_comment: The policy corpus: one baseline document and the mutations that make it refuse.
One baseline rather than twenty near-identical files, because a corpus of copies rots the
day the shape moves — someone 'fixes' it by deleting the cases that broke, and what is left
reads like coverage. Each case is one field set to the wrong thing, so the reason it refuses
is the reason named here and nothing else.
`expect: refuse` cases name the field, and the test demands it. `reason` is asserted only
where this repository wrote the sentence; where the wording belongs to zod the case says
`reasonAlone` and pins the field instead, because a test that asserts a library's phrasing
breaks on a library upgrade and stops testing the rule.
This file is a plain artifact, not CLI-private: a later test may POST every case to
`/v1/policies` and demand that the server refuse exactly the ones the CLI refuses. Two
surfaces, one grammar, and if they ever disagree the corpus is the witness.

meta.name: baseline
meta.description: the smallest policy that means something

cases.name: monthly-cap-in-the-same-unit
cases.comment: the shape `reservedMonthRaw` used to check against nothing

cases.name: never-escalate-is-said-not-implied
cases.comment: an empty requiredWhen is legal and loud; it is not an omission

cases.name: wrapper-form-file
cases.comment: `{ name, document }` is the shape `policy apply` sends, so validate must read it too

cases.name: asset-count-as-a-json-number
cases.comment: NOT an oversight, and this case is what keeps it honest: `decimals` is a `count` (SmallCount, 0-36) while every *amount* is a decimal string. A count cannot be rounded into lying about money; 10^30 wei can. If someone widens SmallCount to cover amounts, or narrows it and breaks this, the case is the witness.

cases.name: limit-unit-mismatch
cases.comment: the accident the compiler exists to refuse: a cap read in one unit against a limit in another

cases.name: transfers-enabled-no-chains
cases.reason: this is a deny, not a policy

cases.name: checksummed-allowlist-entry
cases.comment: the permanent-deny-with-a-friendly-editor case: it compares unequal to every payment

cases.name: wildcard-recipients
cases.comment: S1: the unsafe option is absent from the vocabulary, not deprecated inside it

cases.name: empty-recipient-allowlist
cases.reason: an allowlist with no entries is a deny

cases.name: money-as-a-json-number
cases.comment: the decimal-string rule, and the reason a wei amount cannot be rounded on its way in

cases.name: unknown-field-in-transfers
cases.comment: the field is `perWeek` — a limit the engine will never read, written by someone who believes they added one

cases.name: no-fallback
cases.comment: S15: a policy that does not say what happens when the risk engine is down improvises at the worst moment

cases.name: risk-unavailable-means-allow
cases.comment: the third arm does not exist: deny or escalate, and the bug this repo already fixed was a silent fall-through to allow

cases.name: removed-escalation-condition
cases.comment: `contract_not_in_allowlist` was taken out of the vocabulary because stage 2 already denies it — an option a human can write that does nothing

cases.name: no-approver-roles
cases.comment: an escalation nobody can answer is a payment that stops, and the role list is what makes it answerable

cases.name: chain-not-supported
cases.comment: solana is not in `SupportedChain` at all, so naming it here would be a permission against nothing

cases.name: asset-on-the-wrong-chain
cases.comment: an erc20 on bitcoin: the discriminated union is what refuses it, not a validation callback
